connections.why: Vectors and units underpin all descriptions of motion
Newton's laws relate the motion described to the forces causing it
Work done by forces transfers energy between stores
Circular motion needs a resultant centripetal force
Energy interchanges between kinetic and potential in oscillations
The kinetic model explains temperature and internal energy
Heating is an energy transfer governed by conservation
Charge flow and drift velocity define resistance
Resistance behaviour is applied in circuit analysis
Capacitors charge and discharge through circuit resistances
Gravitational fields supply the centripetal force for orbits
Gravitational field theory underpins planetary and stellar orbits
Stellar measurements feed models of the expanding universe
Basic wave behaviour leads to interference and diffraction
Refraction is one of the core wave behaviours of light
The photon model complements the wave description of light
Laser action depends on photon emission between energy levels
Mass-energy changes in decay explain fission and fusion
Decay processes reveal the fundamental particles involved
Magnetic fields complete the study of fields of force
Changing magnetic flux induces e.m.f. by electromagnetic induction
Capacitors and a.c. theory support the alternating-currents option
